title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-20

ai_review.summary: A jam‑packed second set with stellar Mind Left Body and Truckin' jams captured on a well‑balanced matrix recording.
ai_review.review: The second‑set from this unknown 1973 Denver show is hailed as an “outrageously good” showcase of the band’s improvisational peak, with standout moments like the Mind Left Body jam, a high‑energy Truckin' that feeds into The Other One, and a soaring Stella Blue. Reviewers note the recording is a matrix blend of soundboard clarity and audience ambience – generally clear and well balanced, though a few mention a fuzzy patch in the MLB section. Overall the musical performance far outweighs any minor sonic quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviewers (≈80%) award 4‑5 stars and praise the jams, set flow and overall listening experience; only a handful of low‑star comments relate to rating disputes or minor mix issues, so the combined show + recording score is solidly in the good range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as a nice balance of a clean 73 soundboard with audience ambience; most say it’s crisp and perfect except for a short fuzzy patch in the Mind Left Body jam and a slightly dull high/low end. Overall listeners find it pleasant and well‑balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers rave about the jam‑packed second set – a soaring Truckin' that launches into a bass‑bombed The Other One, followed by an extended Mind Left Body excursion and a beautiful Stella Blue finish. The energy is described as intense, with seamless transitions and thematic jams that embody the peak ‘73 Dead sound.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise Jerry’s tone and guitar work, calling it “intensely pretty” and thanking him for the jam‑heavy performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is highlighted for his explosive “bass bombs” during Truckin' and the deep, natural feel of his lines throughout the set.
